meta.title: GenAI at work — data extraction (Work experiments)
meta.tagline: Study variables, tasks, arms and one result row per arm, measure, subgroup and horizon, every number with its quote and page.
meta.description: Human review of the data extraction for the systematic review of generative AI at work. The model's record is prefilled with a quote behind every value (or empty, for the blind validation sample); the coder checks each task, its arms and its result rows against the highlighted passages, corrects cells, adds or deletes rows, scores the four complexity dimensions blind, and verifies or flags each task. Category fields marked open accept the paper's own term when no category fits. Taxonomy schema b5ed1ca67c; codebook in labeling/codebook.md.

fields.name: screen_ai_treatment
fields.label: Screening 1: AI as the treatment
fields.help: whether a generative AI tool is used while the measured work is produced, compared with the same work done without it (not met when the AI is used only before the measurement as a tutor, feedback tool or practice aid, when both arms use AI, when AI is only the researchers' method, or when it is evaluated on its own with no humans using it)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: screen_work_outcome
fields.label: Screening 2: a work outcome
fields.help: whether an outcome is the output of a work task, or of a task built to emulate one, judged on time, quantity, quality or accuracy (not met: grades and test scores, puzzles that stand for no job, how people worked rather than what they produced, a recipient's health or experience, well-being, attitudes, trust or perceptions alone)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: screen_design
fields.label: Screening 4: an experimental or quasi-experimental design
fields.help: whether the paper compares work done with the AI against work done without it by design: an RCT, a lab or field experiment, a natural or quasi-experiment, a single group before and after (not met: surveys, qualitative or case studies, reviews, theory, descriptive studies, a protocol without results)

options.label: True
options.help: the criterion is met

options.label: False
options.help: clearly not met

options.label: Unclear
options.help: the paper does not let you decide; say why in study_notes

fields.name: scale
fields.label: Scale
fields.help: the level at which the study examines AI's effects, by the primary unit of analysis and the level at which outcomes and conclusions are analysed, not by sample size or setting: a large sample of individual workers is micro; meso only when organisational outcomes are directly examined; macro only when aggregate labour-market or economic outcomes are studied; with several levels, the primary level of the empirical analysis

options.label: Micro
options.help: effects on individuals or small teams: worker productivity, behaviour, skills, task performance, also when the participants work within firms or across several organisations

options.label: Meso
options.help: effects on organisations, firms, workplaces or organisational structures: firm-level productivity, staffing, workflows, organisational performance

options.label: Macro
options.help: effects on labour markets, industries, regions or entire economies: aggregate employment, wages, occupational demand, economy-wide productivity

fields.name: research_design
fields.label: Research design
fields.help: the study's overall empirical design, by how AI exposure is assigned and how the study is organised, for the paper's main with-versus-without-AI comparison; a paper whose tasks differ in design takes the main comparison's, the others noted in task_notes; the estimator goes in identification_strategy

options.label: Lab RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned to AI conditions in a controlled, in-person setting

options.label: Online RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned in an online experiment or web-based setting

options.label: Field RCT
options.help: participants randomly assigned in a real workplace or market

options.label: Natural experiment
options.help: AI exposure arises from an external event or plausibly exogenous variation outside the researchers' control: a launch, a rollout, a policy

options.label: Observational
options.help: naturally occurring AI use or exposure analysed without experimental assignment and without an exogenous event; identification_strategy says how the comparison is made

options.label: Descriptive
options.help: describes AI use or outcomes without a treatment or exposure comparison

fields.name: identification_strategy
fields.label: Identification strategy
fields.help: the primary method used to identify or estimate the causal effect of AI exposure in the main comparison: the actual estimation method, not a broad label such as natural experiment; a specific strategy over generic regression adjustment

options.label: Random assignment
options.help: causal effects identified through randomized treatment assignment

options.label: Difference in differences
options.help: changes in outcomes between treated and comparison groups before and after AI exposure, staggered adoption designs included

options.label: Regression discontinuity
options.help: effects identified at a treatment-assignment threshold

options.label: Instrumental variable
options.help: an instrument that shifts AI exposure but is assumed not to affect outcomes directly

options.label: Interrupted time series
options.help: changes in outcome levels or trends after the AI's introduction, from repeated observations over time

options.label: Matching
options.help: comparable treated and untreated groups constructed on observed characteristics

options.label: Regression adjustment
options.help: statistical controls for observed confounders without a more specific identification strategy

options.label: Pre/post
options.help: outcomes before and after AI adoption without an untreated comparison group

options.label: None
options.help: no causal identification strategy is implemented

fields.name: experimental_design
fields.label: Experimental design
fields.help: whether the same people did the work with and without AI or different people did

options.label: Within person
options.help: the same people do the task with and without the AI

options.label: Across person
options.help: different people in the arms

options.label: Not applicable
options.help: no with-versus-without contrast at the person level

fields.name: unit_of_analysis
fields.label: Unit of analysis
fields.help: the unit the main estimates are computed on

fields.name: data_source
fields.label: Data source
fields.help: the data actually analysed, all that apply; not how participants were recruited or how data were collected: MTurk, Prolific and similar platforms used only for recruitment are neither online_freelancing_data nor online_platform_data

options.label: experimental data
options.help: data generated through a researcher-designed experiment or intervention

options.label: job postings
options.help: job advertisements or vacancy data

options.label: worker - household survey
options.help: survey data from workers, individuals or households, online surveys outside experiments included

options.label: firm survey
options.help: survey data from firms or employers

options.label: public admin data
options.help: government or public administrative records, e.g. Statistics Denmark

options.label: private admin data
options.help: internal firm or private administrative records, e.g. ADP payroll, HR or hiring records

options.label: AI usage data
options.help: observed AI usage or interaction data, e.g. the Anthropic Economic Index, Google ATLAS

options.label: online CVs
options.help: online professional profiles or employment histories, e.g. Revelio, LinkedIn

options.label: online platform data
options.help: observed activity or records from digital platforms, e.g. GitHub

options.label: online freelancing data
options.help: online freelance labour markets: freelancers, contracts, earnings or platform activity, e.g. Upwork, Fiverr

fields.name: period_start_year
fields.label: Data period start, year
fields.help: the year the data begin, as the paper states it

fields.name: period_start_month
fields.label: Data period start, month
fields.help: the month (1-12) the data begin, when the paper gives it; null otherwise

fields.name: period_end_year
fields.label: Data period end, year
fields.help: the year the data end, as the paper states it

fields.name: period_end_month
fields.label: Data period end, month
fields.help: the month (1-12) the data end, when the paper gives it; null otherwise

fields.name: sample_size
fields.label: Sample size
fields.help: the analysed number of human participants in the comparison that establishes the AI effect (the with-versus-without-AI design research_design describes), across its tasks; not a survey, descriptive dataset or pilot in the same paper; with several qualifying studies, the largest; people, never observations, tasks or firms (give those in study_notes); -1 if not stated

fields.name: preregistered
fields.label: Preregistered
fields.help: whether the study was preregistered (a registry, an analysis plan) as the paper states it

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: incentivized
fields.label: Performance incentives
fields.help: whether participants' pay, grade or advancement depended on their performance in the task (performance pay, a bonus, a graded assignment), not merely on taking part; if unclear, default to not_stated

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: vendor_affiliated
fields.label: Vendor affiliated
fields.help: whether an author is affiliated with, or the study was funded or run by, the provider of the AI tool studied (the firm that makes or sells it); read from the title page and the funding note by the coder, which the model does not see

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper does not say

fields.name: focus_topic
fields.label: Focus topic
fields.help: the one topic the paper's stated research question speaks to first; the quote is where the paper states its question

options.label: Inequality
options.help: Findings are about inequality effects of AI.

options.label: Productivity
options.help: Findings are about productivity effects of AI.

options.label: Substitute complement
options.help: Findings relate to the substitutions of humans by AI and/or to AI and humans complementing each other.

options.label: Entry level
options.help: Findings speak to the debate on AI affecting entry-level jobs.

fields.name: focus_topic_secondary
fields.label: Focus topic (secondary)
fields.help: other topics the findings also speak to, each with its own quote; empty when there is none; never other beside a category that fits

options.label: Inequality
options.help: Findings are about inequality effects of AI.

options.label: Productivity
options.help: Findings are about productivity effects of AI.

options.label: Substitute complement
options.help: Findings relate to the substitutions of humans by AI and/or to AI and humans complementing each other.

options.label: Entry level
options.help: Findings speak to the debate on AI affecting entry-level jobs.

fields.name: focus_dimension
fields.label: Focus dimension
fields.help: whether the study focuses on workers (supply) or on employers' demand for labour (demand); both only when both are explicitly studied. Default to supply for worker-focused studies, including most AI productivity and collaboration experiments; never infer demand from productivity gains, economic outcomes or possible employment implications; demand only when employer labour demand is directly examined. Quote the paper's own statement of its question or findings, never a cited work

options.label: Demand
options.help: only studies explicitly examining employers' labour requirements: job postings, vacancies, recruitment, hiring patterns, skill demand, workforce expansion or reduction

options.label: Supply
options.help: any study about workers: their tasks, skills, behaviour, AI use, productivity, performance, wages or employment outcomes, including experiments with individuals, professionals or teams doing work tasks

fields.name: peer_reviewed
fields.label: Peer reviewed
fields.help: filled in code from the record's venue and the predatory-journal list, not by the model

fields.name: summary
fields.label: Summary
fields.help: four to eight sentences stating the paper's main findings with their numbers, in plain language; written by the summary call, nothing that is not in the paper

fields.name: model_estimands
fields.label: Model estimands
fields.help: what the model found the paper estimates: one row per task, arm against reference arm, outcome, subgroup and horizon, with the coder's match verdict

columns.name: match
columns.label: Match
columns.help: your verdict on the model's estimand

options.label: Matched
options.help: one of your outcomes: give its id in coder_outcome

options.label: model only, keep
options.help: an outcome you missed and the paper reports: add it to your outcomes

options.label: model only, drop
options.help: the paper does not estimate this

options.label: Unsure
options.help: say why in the note

columns.name: coder_task
columns.label: Your task
columns.help: the id of your task (T1 …) this estimand belongs to

columns.name: coder_arm
columns.label: Your arm
columns.help: the id of your arm (T1 …) that is compared with the reference

columns.name: coder_outcome
columns.label: Your outcome
columns.help: the id of your outcome (O1 …) this estimand belongs to

fields.name: model_estimates
fields.label: Model estimates
fields.help: the model's estimates, one per estimand and specification with the cell they were read from; ＋ row accepts one as a result row

options.label: Main
options.help: the estimate the authors lead with for this estimand

options.label: Supporting
options.help: another specification presented alongside

options.label: Robustness
options.help: a check: appendix, alternative estimator, restriction

options.label: reference arm
options.help: the reference arm's printed statistics for this estimand

options.label: Orphan
options.help: a number in an exhibit the model could not place

columns.name: source
columns.label: Source
columns.help: the exhibit, panel, column and row the numbers were read from

columns.name: flags
columns.label: Checks
columns.help: what the deterministic checks found on this estimate before import (a number not in its cell or quote, a standard error that differs from the table, a duplicate cell, instability across runs); blank when none

columns.name: verdict
columns.label: Verdict
columns.help: your verdict after checking the cell in the PDF

options.label: Accepted
options.help: checked against the PDF and taken as a result row (＋ row)

options.label: Wrong
options.help: a number or its mapping is wrong: say what in the note

options.label: Duplicate
options.help: the same estimate as another row

options.label: not an estimate
options.help: not an estimate of a with-versus-without-AI contrast

options.label: Unsure
options.help: say why in the note

fields.name: evidence_statements
fields.label: Evidence statements
fields.help: one row per finding of the summary: the finding in one sentence with the number as printed, backed by the quoted passage; result_ref names the result row it rests on as task_id/arm_id/measure, or is null for a finding with no row

fields.name: study_notes
fields.label: Study notes
fields.help: anything a coder must know about the paper as a whole: several studies, exclusions, discrepancies between text and tables

fields.name: evidence_items
fields.label: Evidence items
fields.help: the numbered passages and tables the reader took from the methods and results, one row each in the order they appear; bears_on names the fields the reader thought the item supports

columns.name: text
columns.label: Text
columns.help: the passage verbatim; for a table its caption and rows as markdown

entries.label: Task
entries.help: one per distinct task the participants performed, with its arms (the reference arm included) and its result rows
entries.title: {task_id} · {task_name}

fields.name: task_id
fields.label: Task id
fields.help: T1, T2, ... in the order the paper presents the tasks; S2.T1 when the paper's studies are numbered and repeat tasks

fields.name: task_name
fields.label: Task name
fields.help: a short unique name for the task made from the paper's description: 'classification of chest X-rays', 'mid-level professional writing', 'customer support chats'

fields.name: task_label
fields.label: Task label
fields.help: the category the core activity of the task falls in. The label follows the purpose of the output, not its medium ('analyse a complaint and draft a written analysis' is problem_solving_reasoning, writing being only the medium; 'write a blog post' is writing), and the specific category wins over the generic one (persuasion_negotiation, advising_recommending, summarizing_synthesis, forecasting, customer_interaction before writing, data_analysis or problem_solving_reasoning); writing only when the text itself is the product

options.label: Writing
options.help: Producing new prose text from scratch. E.g., drafting a cover letter, press release or essay.

options.label: Editing & Feedback
options.help: Improving existing text or work, or giving written feedback on it. E.g., revising a draft for clarity, giving peer feedback on an essay.

options.label: Summarizing & synthesis
options.help: Condensing or integrating given source material into a shorter account that stays faithful to the sources. E.g., summarizing a report, synthesizing findings from several papers.

options.label: Translation
options.help: Translating from one language into another while preserving the meaning.

options.label: Programming
options.help: Writing, modifying, debugging or testing code.

options.label: Data analysis
options.help: Processing and analyzing quantitative data to produce results, models or insights. E.g., running a regression, building a spreadsheet model.

options.label: Information search
options.help: Finding information from external sources to answer questions. E.g.,searching the web.

options.label: Problem solving & reasoning
options.help: Solving problems through reasoning. E.g., math problems, logic puzzles, exam questions.

options.label: Classification & detection
options.help: Assigning items to predefined categories. E.g., labelling X-rays as normal/abnormal, flagging fake news.

options.label: Evaluation & selection
options.help: Judging the quality of items or choosing among options, where no predefined category scheme exists. E.g., screening CVs, grading essays, picking an investment.

options.label: Forecasting
options.help: Predicting future outcomes or unknown quantities. E.g., predicting recidivism, forecasting sales.

options.label: Ideation
options.help: Generating new ideas or concepts. E.g., brainstorming product or business ideas.

options.label: Visual design
options.help: Creating visual artifacts. E.g., illustrations, UI mockups, slides.

options.label: Advising & recommending
options.help: Producing a recommendation tailored to a specific person's or organization's situation. E.g., a treatment plan, legal advice, a consulting recommendation.

options.label: Customer interaction
options.help: Real-time, conversational service with clients or customers. E.g., support chats.

options.label: Planning & scheduling
options.help: Producing a plan, schedule or allocation of resources over time. E.g., a project plan, event itinerary, shift schedule.

options.label: Persuasion & negotiation
options.help: Producing messages or bargaining behavior aimed at changing another party's beliefs, decisions or terms. E.g., writing a convincing message, negotiating a deal.

options.label: Physical & manual tasks
options.help: catch all for tasks where the core activity is bodily work or handling physical objects, materials or equipment. E.g., assembling components, operating machinery, providing hands-on patient care.

fields.name: soc_major_group
fields.label: SOC major group
fields.help: the occupation the task belongs to (the work, not the participants): a legal memo is Legal (23) whoever writes it; not_applicable when none fits

options.label: Arts, Design, Entertainment, Sports, and Media (27)
Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance (37)
Not applicable
options.help: Anything not fitting above.

fields.name: task_structure
fields.label: Task structure
fields.help: closed when there is a verifiable right answer, open_ended when the output is quality-rated

options.label: Closed
options.help: scored by accuracy against a unambiguous solution

options.label: open-ended
options.help: quality-rated

fields.name: task_embodiment
fields.label: Embodiment
fields.help: whether the task needs physical presence: remote unless the task requires face-to-face interaction (co_present) or bodily work (physical)

options.label: remote - disembodied
options.help: task can be done with no need for physical presence, e.g. remotely via a computer (or phone)

options.label: Co-present
options.help: The task requires physical presence, mainly because it involves face-to-face interaction with people, but not manual work. E.g., teaching a class, conducting a patient consultation, in-store sales.

options.label: Physical
options.help: The task requires bodily work or the handling of physical objects, materials or equipment.

fields.name: task_notes
fields.label: Task notes
fields.help: what a coder must know about the task: what participants did when the name does not say it, how arms map to the paper's conditions, a design that differs from the study's design_type, in a reversed design the worker the AI replaces, discrepancies

fields.name: k_score
fields.label: Knowledge & education: complex?
fields.help: Knowledge and Education: is the task complex on this dimension? Yes or No by the rubric (the options carry the criteria); mark in the PDF the sentences the score rests on. If scaffolding substantially lowered the bar (worked examples, cheat-sheets, procedure-recall tools), score based on what participants actually had to bring after the scaffolding. Programming note: it is the depth of programming knowledge that matters, not the language name. Intro courses teach Python, Java, or C — but professional uses often require more than basics to use these languages effectively. Do not score a language as first-year simply because it appears in introductory curricula.

options.label: Yes
options.help: the task requires second-year undergraduate knowledge or above. That is at least some degree of specialization within knowledge domain.

options.label: No
options.help: high-school or first-year undergraduate knowledge suffices, including basic undergraduate concepts.

fields.name: g_score
fields.label: Goal & path: complex?
fields.help: Goal Definition and Path Specification: is the task complex on this dimension? Yes or No by the rubric (the options carry the criteria); mark in the PDF the sentences the score rests on. Subjective or holistic grading is evidence of openness but not sufficient on its own — a concrete problem with an easy-to-infer route, rated holistically (e.g. "resolve this customer's issue," scored by CSAT), is still No. A clean outcome metric does not make a task closed if the route to it is hard to infer.

options.label: Yes
options.help: the path to completion is hard to infer: it is not obvious how to proceed from the stated objective, OR there are many valid approaches / no single right answer, so it is easy to get lost or commit to a wrong route. Importantly, in getting lost there should be a mistake that makes the task fail. This includes tasks whose end-state and metric are perfectly clear but whose route is undiscovered and tasks where it is hard to identify what the objective even is. For example "improve firm profit," "get rich," "win the game", are all tasks whose route is hard to discover and the wrong path would cause a failure (e.g. company default or losing the game).

options.label: No
options.help: how to proceed is easy to infer, even if the instruction does not spell it out: a determinate done-state with an obvious or readily-found route and little risk of getting lost (a defined deliverable against a key or rubric, a specific problem with a specified target).

fields.name: i_score
fields.label: Interdependence: complex?
fields.help: Task Interdependence: is the task complex on this dimension? Yes or No by the rubric (the options carry the criteria); mark in the PDF the sentences the score rests on. Three rules: - Trivial decomposition is not interdependence. "You must do A before B" holds almost everywhere and is not the target. Score Yes only when the parts are of different nature and an early error is genuinely hard to spot and costly to undo. - Easy, timely correction defeats coupling. Fast, reliable feedback (a counterpart who corrects you, a rerunnable test, visible intermediate results) → No. Slow, noisy, or confounded feedback (a market signal weeks later) does not count. - Programming tasks: distinguish compile-time from deployment feedback. Compilers/tests catch syntax and unit-level errors quickly, but multi-day/multi-week projects surface the relevant feedback at integration or deployment — slow and noisy. A 1-hour task with a rerunnable test suite → No; an ongoing project where errors surface at launch or in downstream systems → Yes. - Do not score from the grading structure. A conjunctive grade ("pass all 12") or a single holistic score is a measurement property, not task structure; ignore it.

options.label: Yes
options.help: the task combines genuinely *different* kinds of subtask, AND an error in an early or upstream component is *hard to catch as the work proceeds* and *likely to propagate or be costly to fix* — often forcing a partial restart rather than a local patch. The heart of the dimension is that mistakes are hard to detect mid-task and expensive to unwind, not that recovery is strictly impossible.

options.label: No
options.help: the work is either (a) a stream of independent or repeated homogeneous units (one chat after another, paragraph after paragraph), where an error stays local; or (b) coupled but where errors are *easy to catch and cheap to fix as you go* — a counterpart redirects you, you rerun a test, you see intermediate output and revise before completion.

fields.name: r_score
fields.label: Resources & context: complex?
fields.help: Resources and Context: is the task complex on this dimension? Yes or No by the rubric (the options carry the criteria); mark in the PDF the sentences the score rests on. Do not count the AI tool being studied as a resource — it is the treatment.

options.label: Yes
options.help: the task requires substantial resources beyond what is handed to the participant: extensive materials to search or synthesise across a large context (e.g. a corpus of documents, multiple studies to browse, a large codebase, browsing the internet for at least an hour), specialist data sources or tools, or substantial context-specific knowledge — whether firm-specific (e.g. tacit knowledge), study-specific, procedural, or otherwise — that the participant must bring or that would need to be supplied to a model.

options.label: No
options.help: the task is self-contained: a few materials sitting directly in front of the participant suffice, and it draws only on general knowledge or basic everyday tacit knowledge.

children.label: Arm
children.help: one per condition of the task, the reference arm first
children.title: {arm_id} · {arm_label}

fields.name: arm_id
fields.label: Arm id
fields.help: C for the reference arm, T1, T2, ... for the treatment arms of this task, in the paper's order

fields.name: arm_label
fields.label: Arm label
fields.help: the paper's own name for the condition ('Control', 'ChatGPT access', 'GPT-4 + overview')

fields.name: is_baseline
fields.label: Reference arm
fields.help: true for the one arm of the task the others are compared with: usually the people doing the work without the AI, or before getting it; control_type says what the comparison is

fields.name: compared_with
fields.label: Compared with
fields.help: the arm_id of the reference arm this arm is compared with; empty when the task has one reference arm (then every other arm is compared with it)

fields.name: control_type
fields.label: Control type
fields.help: what the reference arm is, on the reference arm only (null on the treatment arms)

options.label: no AI, concurrent group
options.help: a concurrent group or condition doing the task without the AI, drawn from the same pool (randomized or assigned; design_type says which)

options.label: no AI, the same units before
options.help: the same people or units before access: a pre-period, an own baseline, the not-yet-treated state of a rollout

options.label: no AI, the same units after
options.help: the same people or units after the AI was taken away (a ban, an outage, the end of access): the time or group with the AI is the treatment arm, the one without it the reference arm, whatever the paper calls the treatment

options.label: another, non-AI tool
options.help: the comparison condition got a non-AI aid instead: a search engine, documentation, templates, a checklist, non-generative software

options.label: another AI
options.help: a different AI system or configuration is the comparison (an older model, no retrieval, a different prompt or interface, non-agentic); every arm uses AI

options.label: expert benchmark
options.help: unassisted experts or incumbents whose performance is the reference for AI-assisted others: a different population, not an assigned condition

options.label: the AI alone
options.help: the AI's own output with no human; recorded only when the paper's contrast is against it, with n_arm null

options.label: external norm
options.help: a published norm, a historical rate or a market benchmark; no participants

options.label: None
options.help: no comparison: a single arm, descriptive

fields.name: sample_population
fields.label: Sample population
fields.help: who the people in this arm are, in the paper's own words: 'BCG consultants', 'third-year law students', 'customer support agents of a Fortune 500 firm'

fields.name: sample_population_type
fields.label: Population type
fields.help: the kind of people the outcomes are measured on: the actual population whose outcomes are measured, not everyone the study mentions. The specific category wins over the generic one; recruitment through an online platform or panel takes precedence over general_population whatever the age, nationality or demographic restrictions; never other merely because a sample is heterogeneous or distinctively described

options.label: Students
options.help: university or school students

options.label: crowdworkers/online panel
options.help: Prolific, MTurk, similar platforms

options.label: general population
options.help: members of the public or of sub-populations: convenience samples, job applicants, mixed groups of adults without a shared task-relevant occupation

options.label: Professionals, in-domain
options.help: People working in the occupation the task comes from such as consultants on consulting tasks, radiologists on X-ray

options.label: Professionals, out-of-domain
options.help: Professionals doing a task outside their field

options.label: recipients of the work
options.help: the people the work is for, when the outcomes are measured on them: patients counselled, customers served, students taught (a reversed design, see the rules)

fields.name: sample_expertise
fields.label: Expertise
fields.help: the arm's training and experience in the domain of the task, decided in this order: (1) people employed in the occupation the task belongs to are expert, whatever their seniority and whatever spread of skill or experience the paper reports among them, unless the paper itself calls them junior, then intermediate; (2) students in the field and trainees are intermediate; (3) people with no training in the domain (the general public, crowdworkers, job applicants, students outside the field) are novice; (4) mixed only when the arm deliberately combines people from different levels in this sense (students with professionals, laypeople with experts), never for a reported skill spread within one occupational sample; (5) not_applicable only for a task with no domain anyone could be trained in (a hidden-profile game, a generic survey); (6) not_stated when the paper says nothing about who the people are

options.label: Novice
options.help: no training in the task domain: the general public, crowdworkers, job applicants, students outside the field; a sample described as needing no specific industry or contextual knowledge

options.label: Intermediate
options.help: students in the field, trainees, and staff the paper itself calls junior

options.label: Expert
options.help: employed in the occupation the task belongs to, whatever the seniority or the spread of skill the paper reports, unless the paper itself calls them junior

options.label: Mixed
options.help: the arm deliberately combines people from different levels (students with professionals, laypeople with experts); a reported spread of skill or experience within one occupational sample is not mixed

options.label: Not applicable
options.help: the task has no domain anyone could be trained in

options.label: not stated
options.help: the paper gives no information on who the people are

fields.name: sample_representativeness
fields.label: Representativeness
fields.help: how the arm's sample relates to a population

options.label: Population-wide
options.help: e.g. register data in Denmark

options.label: representative sample
options.help: e.g. household or firm survey

options.label: non-representative sample
options.help: e.g. small experiment

fields.name: countries
fields.label: Countries
fields.help: where the arm's people or data come from, not the authors; 'online, unspecified' when the paper does not say

fields.name: n_arm
fields.label: People in the arm
fields.help: human subjects who did this task in this arm; null if not stated

fields.name: arm_description
fields.label: What this arm got
fields.help: tool, access, training, prompts, restrictions: what made this condition what it was

fields.name: arm_notes
fields.label: Arm notes
fields.help: anything a coder must know about the arm

fields.name: ai_model
fields.label: AI model
fields.help: the exact system this arm used, with version and access route ('GPT-4 via ChatGPT Plus', 'GitHub Copilot', 'Claude Sonnet 4'); null for a no-AI reference arm or if not stated

fields.name: ai_role
fields.label: AI role
fields.help: how the AI took part in the work in this arm; none for a no-AI reference arm

options.label: Open-ended assistance
options.help: the human has open-ended access and uses it however they like; a general-purpose chatbot or agent is open_ended_assistance

options.label: AI review
options.help: The human produces the work and AI provides feedback.

options.label: AI advice
options.help: AI gives a recommendation like a prediction or a label but human makes decision. E.g. radiology image classification or algorithmic hiring

options.label: Human review
options.help: AI produces the work and the human reviews it.

options.label: AI-only
options.help: Full delegation with human limited to prompting, guiding and giving feedback.

options.label: None
options.help: the arm did not use AI (a no-AI reference arm)

fields.name: is_agentic
fields.label: Agentic tool
fields.help: whether the AI autonomously executes a multi-step task or workflow rather than merely responding or assisting: true when it independently determines and executes successive actions toward a goal (conducting an interview, navigating software, using tools, modifying files, completing a workflow with limited human intervention); false when it responds to individual prompts, generates content, recommends or assists without executing a sequence of actions on its own; null for a no-AI reference arm

fields.name: ai_measure
fields.label: How AI enters
fields.help: how AI exposure or use is operationalised in this arm; null for a no-AI reference arm

options.label: Exposure
options.help: potential exposure to AI measured through an index, score or proxy based on tasks, occupations or capabilities, e.g. Eloundou et al.

options.label: Adoption
options.help: actual AI adoption or deployment by workers, firms or organisations, naturally occurring rollouts included, where adoption is not assigned by the researchers

options.label: observed usage
options.help: actual intensity, frequency or patterns of AI use measured through usage logs, interactions or other behavioural records

options.label: experimental access
options.help: the researchers assign, provide or withhold access to AI as part of an experimental intervention, whether or not the participants use it

children.label: Outcome
children.help: one per measure the task is scored on, the coder's list
children.title: {outcome_id} · {outcome_finding}

fields.name: outcome_id
fields.label: Outcome id
fields.help: O1, O2 … in the paper's order

fields.name: outcome_name
fields.label: Measure
fields.help: the outcome as the paper names it: 'time taken', 'average grade'

fields.name: how_measured
fields.label: How measured
fields.help: who or what produced the measure and against what standard: blinded professional graders on a 1-7 rubric, self-reported minutes, a timer

fields.name: outcome_unit
fields.label: Unit
fields.help: the unit or scale of the measure as printed: 'minutes', '1-7 scale', 'percent correct', 'USD', 'count'; null when the paper gives none

fields.name: outcome_direction
fields.label: Better side
fields.help: up if higher values are better (quality, output); down if lower is better (time, errors); neutral for a quantity without a better side

fields.name: outcome_type
fields.label: Outcome class
fields.help: what kind of outcome the measure is, by what was measured and not by its name; every outcome measured while the treatment arm has the AI in use, with a with-versus-without-AI contrast, is a row; an outcome measured afterwards without the AI (a post-test, a retention test, later unaided work) is not a row: name it in task_notes

options.label: work performance
options.help: the work produced or the task performed, measured by graders, instruments, timers, counts or an answer key: time, output volume, quality, accuracy, errors, completion, creativity or novelty rated by others

options.label: Behaviour
options.help: what people did, observed: use or adoption of the AI, reliance on or acceptance of its suggestions, take-up of the assigned condition, time allocation across tasks, effort, help-seeking, collaboration

options.label: subjective report
options.help: what people reported about themselves or the work: satisfaction, enjoyment, well-being, stress, perceived agency or autonomy, trust, confidence, self-assessed performance, beliefs, attitudes, intentions

options.label: labour market
options.help: employment status, retention or attrition, earnings, hours, promotion, hiring

fields.name: outcome_finding
fields.label: Finding type
fields.help: the finer kind of outcome this row measures

options.label: Time taken
options.help: time to complete a piece of work, or output per period: durations, counts per period, throughput, completion share

options.label: Output quality
options.help: the quality of the work: ratings on a scale, pass or acceptance rates, error and revision counts

options.label: Employment or hiring
options.help: employment status, hiring, retention or attrition as the outcome

options.label: Wages or earnings
options.help: pay, earnings or income as the outcome

options.label: Labour demand
options.help: demand for workers or for a kind of work: vacancies, postings, hours demanded

options.label: Skill split
options.help: Lower- vs higher-skill effect

options.label: Task shift
options.help: Change in share/volume of a kind of work

options.label: Output diversity
options.help: Collective output diversity across people or items

options.label: Performance dispersion
options.help: the spread of performance across people: a slope by baseline skill, a variance, a correlation across tasks

options.label: Adoption or usage of the AI
options.help: adoption or usage of AI as the outcome

options.label: Secondary outcome
options.help: well-being, attitudes, beliefs, trust

fields.name: outcome_measure_kind
fields.label: Measure kind
fields.help: for a performance outcome, what the measure counts: one level below the finding type, which follows from it (durations, counts per period, throughput and completion shares are time taken; ratings, pass rates and error counts are quality; a dispersion statistic is dispersion); null for an outcome of another class

options.label: duration per task or work item
options.help: time to complete a defined piece of work: minutes per task, handle time, hours to completion, time to reply

options.label: output count per period
options.help: pieces of work completed in a period: pull requests, commits, documents, emails replied to

options.label: throughput rate
options.help: output per unit of time: resolutions per hour, chats per hour

options.label: completion share or composite index
options.help: the share of a task completed, or a quality-over-time index

options.label: rating on a scale
options.help: quality judged by graders, experts or a model on a scale: a 1 to 7 quality score, a 4.0 grade, creativity, coherence

options.label: pass, acceptance or resolution rate
options.help: the share of work that meets a standard: correctness, build success, approval, resolution

options.label: error and revision counts
options.help: defects or rework counted on the output: hallucinations, review comments, merge conflicts

options.label: dispersion between workers
options.help: a statistic of the spread of performance across people: a slope by baseline skill, a variance, a correlation of grades across tasks

fields.name: outcome_measured_on
fields.label: Measured on
fields.help: whom or what the measure is taken on

options.label: the worker
options.help: the person doing the task: their time, throughput, errors, use of the tool, self-reports

options.label: the output
options.help: the work product, graded by others or against a key

options.label: the recipient
options.help: the person the work is for: a patient's comprehension of a consultation, a customer's satisfaction with the service

fields.name: contrast_type
fields.label: Contrast type
fields.help: what the effect compares; null on a reference-arm row

options.label: AI vs no AI
options.help: an AI arm against a no-AI reference arm (concurrent or placebo tool)

options.label: post vs pre
options.help: the same units after getting the AI against before

options.label: AI vs AI
options.help: two AI arms against each other (two tools, two models)

options.label: AI variant
options.help: an AI arm against the same AI with a feature, prompt or interface changed

options.label: Dose
options.help: more versus less use or access to the same AI

options.label: vs benchmark
options.help: an arm against a benchmark that is not a condition of the study: unassisted experts, a published norm

options.label: human+AI vs AI alone
options.help: people using the AI against the AI's own output with no human

options.label: Interaction
options.help: the difference between two subgroups' AI effects

options.label: Association
options.help: users against non-users without assignment

fields.name: estimand_type
fields.label: Estimand
fields.help: which effect the row estimates, by how people entered the comparison; null on a reference-arm row

options.label: intent to treat
options.help: by assigned condition, whether or not the tool was used

options.label: treatment on the treated
options.help: the effect for those who used the tool, with assignment as the instrument (LATE, TOT)

options.label: per protocol
options.help: users or compliers only, by actual use, without instrumenting

options.label: not applicable
options.help: no assignment: an observational association or a descriptive comparison

fields.name: subgroup
fields.label: Subgroup
fields.help: 'full sample', or the subset this row is for: of people ('bottom half of baseline ability'), of tasks ('routine topics'), of sites, of time since treatment

fields.name: horizon
fields.label: Horizon
fields.help: when the outcome is measured relative to AI access: 'same session', '8 weeks after rollout'; null if a single cross-section

fields.name: statistic
fields.label: Statistic
fields.help: what the central value in `mean` is

fields.name: n
fields.label: n
fields.help: people (or units) behind this row's value

fields.name: n_obs
fields.label: Observations
fields.help: the observations behind the estimate when they differ from the people (tasks x participants, person-weeks, tickets), as printed; null when equal to n or not stated

fields.name: cluster_level
fields.label: Clustered on
fields.help: what the standard errors are clustered on ('participant', 'team', 'branch'), as stated; null if not clustered or not stated

fields.name: mean
fields.label: Mean
fields.help: the arm's central value of the measure as printed, whichever statistic the paper gives (`statistic` says which); a proportion as printed (0.82 or 82, not converted)

fields.name: sd
fields.label: SD
fields.help: the arm's standard deviation as printed; from an SE or CI only with estimated = true and the arithmetic in result_notes; for a median, null with the IQR in result_notes

fields.name: effect_reported
fields.label: Effect as reported
fields.help: the number exactly as printed, with its sign and unit: '-40%', '+0.41 SD', '0.18 (0.05)'; null on a reference-arm row

fields.name: effect_value
fields.label: Effect value
fields.help: the same number as a plain number in the units of effect_type; null if the paper gives only a direction

fields.name: effect_type
fields.label: Effect type
fields.help: the form of the number in effect_value

fields.name: effect_units
fields.label: Effect units
fields.help: 'minutes', 'percent of the control mean', 'SD of the pre-treatment grade', 'log points'

fields.name: se
fields.label: SE
fields.help: standard error as printed

fields.name: ci_low
fields.label: CI low
fields.help: lower 95% bound as printed

fields.name: ci_high
fields.label: CI high
fields.help: upper 95% bound as printed

fields.name: p_value
fields.label: p
fields.help: as a number, as printed; null if only stars or an inequality

fields.name: p_reported
fields.label: p as printed
fields.help: the significance exactly as printed when p_value cannot hold it: '<0.01', 'p = .03', '***' (with the note's star convention); null otherwise

fields.name: estimated
fields.label: Estimated
fields.help: true if any value in the row was read from a figure or computed rather than printed; say how in result_notes

fields.name: is_main
fields.label: Main estimate
fields.help: true for the paper's main specification of this measure: the estimate the results section leads with (the main table's full-sample row), not a robustness check, an alternative estimator or a secondary specification; at most one per estimand

fields.name: source
fields.label: Source
fields.help: 'Table 2, column 3', 'Figure 1', 'p. 5 text'

fields.name: outcome
fields.label: Outcome
fields.help: the id (O1 …) of the outcome in the coder's outcomes list

fields.name: estimate
fields.label: Estimate
fields.help: the id of the model estimate this row was accepted from; empty for a row added by hand

fields.name: result_notes
fields.label: Result notes
fields.help: derivations, which specification, caveats

groups.label: Design
groups.help: scale, research and identification design, data source, unit of analysis, sample size, period

groups.label: Task
groups.help: what the task was, its category, occupation and work activities

groups.label: Complexity
groups.help: the four descriptive fields the complexity scores are given from

groups.label: Arm
groups.help: the conditions of the task: what the reference arm is, who the arm's people are, the tool and its role, what the arm got

groups.label: Results
groups.help: the result rows: measure, subgroup, horizon, the numbers and their quotes
